scores.evidence: Flink job definition runs both live and in backfill mode. Every scored feature vector is also logged (log-and-wait) for future training
scores.rationale: Mostly accurate (tokenization, SAD dropped, out-of-time splits, label delay, acks=all), with minor imprecision like 'Flink backfill reproduces live values' and the 'Kafka acks=all plus local disk buffer' that have no design consequence.

scores.evidence: I've assumed we are an issuer or issuer-processor scoring inline in authorization, so a decline is possible.
scores.rationale: Resolves the ambiguity explicitly with consequences if wrong, covers core needs, and defers step-up, multi-region and others with reasons and pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: The auth host stays system of record for the auth decision. The existing rules stay as champion and fallback; the new scorer is the challenger.
scores.rationale: Consistent ownership and data flow; minor loose ends such as a step-up action in the policy mention versus deferral and analyst-managed rule hot-deploy not detailed.

scores.evidence: In 100% of ≥ 1,000 injections per fault type, the auth host returns the champion decision inside its timeout.
scores.rationale: Validation checks V0–V8 are tied to specific risks, run early (skeleton, fault injection, parity), have labeled provisional thresholds, and continue in production via holdout, drift and canary.

scores.evidence: Missing inputs (most plan-changing first): 1. Where we sit in the flow, and inline vs post-auth.
scores.rationale: Assumptions are labeled ASSUMPTION/BASELINE/UNKNOWN, ranked by plan impact, with explicit consequences and how they are confirmed.

scores.evidence: Label review against poisoning: "friendly fraud" (cardholders disputing purchases they made), insider label edits.
scores.rationale: Covers fail-closed mass declines, breaker, queue overflow, card-testing bursts, attacker-controlled inputs, poisoning, feature store outage and Kafka outage with detection and recovery; duplicates/reversals are thinner.

scores.evidence: Deployed by CI/CD (signed image, Helm canary) into the CDE segment... Rollback is `helm rollback`, or the auth-host flag off
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback, alerts, on-call, two-person config approval and runbook drills are concrete; incident ownership details and team sizing are light.

scores.evidence: Storage cost / retention | UNKNOWN. Missing input: how long decision and feature logs must be kept.
scores.rationale: Build-vs-buy is considered and CPU in-process serving is chosen, but there is no cost estimate, no scaling cost analysis for Flink/Redis/storage, and no concrete cost controls.

scores.evidence: | Sync vs async | R2: the auth integration contract needs coordinated work across teams |
scores.rationale: Each decision carries reversibility class, validator and revisit trigger; identifier schema is validated before hardening; rules engine kept, decommissioning flagged as the point of no return; vendor seam behind same API.

scores.evidence: one decision-service deployable (features, model and policy in one process, with no extra network hops on the hot path)
scores.rationale: Mostly proportionate with simplest hot path and deferrals, but there is heavy process ceremony (V0–V8, seven phases, dependency tables) and an irrelevant 'AI layer' sublayer table.

scores.evidence: Exit check (V0): a real test-BIN authorization succeeds with one trace across every tier. A deploy and a rollback succeed through the pipeline.
scores.rationale: Thin end-to-end slice first, dependency-justified phase order, checkable exit criteria per phase, and fallback plans when checks fail.

checklist.evidence: p99 ≤ 50 ms; the auth host gives up at 80 ms and falls back
Fall back to the current decision (existing rules plus auth host). Never decline because the scorer timed out or errored
One Flink job definition runs both live and in backfill mode.
Out-of-time backtest on the latest 3 matured months (labels ≥ 90 days old)
At equal decline rate, ≥ 10% more fraud value caught than champion BASELINE; false-positive ratio ≤ BASELINE
Policy layer combining rules and model thresholds into an action from the allowed list: APPROVE, APPROVE+CASE, or DECLINE+CASE.
Case queue in case management. If the queue overflows, transactions are approved with an alert, never declined.
The pipeline sees only a PAN token plus BIN. Sensitive authentication data (CVV, track data, PIN data) is dropped at ingress
online state rebuilt from Kafka replay within the RTO
Drift monitors: PSI (population stability index) per feature and on the score. Monthly retrain producing a challenger that goes through shadow
every decision records model and policy version
3× peak authorizations per second, sustained for 1 h

traps.evidence: A synchronous gRPC score call inside authorization with an 80 ms hard timeout.
Never decline because the scorer timed out or errored
Out-of-time backtest on the latest 3 matured months (labels ≥ 90 days old)
V4 | Backfilled features equal the features served live
zero PAN or sensitive-auth-data matches in either scan

note: Exceptionally rigorous, risk-driven plan with inline latency budget, safe fallback, staged shadow/canary rollout and reversibility analysis. Weaknesses are missing cost analysis, thin stream event-correctness detail, and deferred step-up and multi-region.
